introduce: Ginnethon is the name of a priestly family that appears in Nehemiah 12 (Nehemiah 12:4, 16).
biblecontents: In the list of the heads of the priestly families in the time of Joiakim, it appears as "of the clan of Ginnethon, Meshullam" (Nehemiah 12:12, 16).
history: It is one of the lists of priestly families that returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, and forms part of a historical document recording the genealogy and offices of the priests who took part in the dedication of the wall at that time.

introduce: Nahath is a personal name that appears in the list of the chiefs of the Edomite clans and in the genealogy of a Levite; it is a case of use as an individual's name, rather than as a place name referring to a particular region.
biblecontents: According to Genesis 36:13, Nahath is mentioned as one of the sons of Reuel, the son of Esau, and is recorded as one of the chiefs of Edom (Genesis 36:13). His name is likewise found as a son of Reuel in 1 Chronicles 1:37 (1 Chronicles 1:37). Also, in 1 Chronicles 6:26 Nahath appears as one of the Levites who were descendants of Kohath (1 Chronicles 6:26). Finally, in 2 Chronicles 31:13 Nahath is mentioned as one of the overseers who managed the temple offerings in the time of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 31:13).

introduce: The Nethinim is the name for a group of lower-ranking servants who were set apart in ancient Israelite society to carry out the menial tasks of the temple. They were originally made up of foreigners who were not Israelites, but after the return from the Babylonian exile they came to hold a position as a particular class devoted exclusively to the service of the temple.
biblecontents: The Nethinim lived in their own cities together with the Israelites, the priests, and the Levites (1 Chronicles 9:2). Among those who returned with Zerubbabel at the return from the Babylonian exile, the descendants of the Nethinim were the descendants of Ziha, the descendants of Hasupha, the descendants of Tabbaoth, and so on (Ezra 2:43). The total number of them together with the descendants of Solomon's servants was 392 (Ezra 2:58). The people, the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim settled in their cities (Ezra 2:70). Among those who went up to Jerusalem with Ezra in the time of King Artaxerxes were also some of the Nethinim (Ezra 7:7). The king exempted the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim from the payment of tribute or customs duty (Ezra 7:24). Ezra sent men to the region of Casiphia and asked the Nethinim there to bring servants for the temple (Ezra 8:17). The 220 Nethinim were those whom David and the officials had given to help the Levites (Ezra 8:20). The Nethinim lived in Ophel and made repairs as far as the gate on its north side (Nehemiah 3:26). They repaired the wall as far as the gate opposite the temple and the room at the corner of the city wall (Nehemiah 3:31).
geography: After the return from the exile, the Nethinim lived in the Ophel area within Jerusalem, which means a geographical position adjacent to the temple precincts (Nehemiah 3:26). The rest of them lived scattered through the various cities of Israel (Ezra 2:70).
history: The name Nethinim derives from the Hebrew nathan (to give) and carries the meaning "those given to the temple." In ancient Israelite history they are presumed to be descendants of those who, like the Gibeonites, were taken as prisoners of war and designated to do menial work such as cutting wood and drawing water for the temple. This class, which existed even before the exile, was reorganized after the return from the Babylonian exile, in the course of the religious reforms of Ezra and Nehemiah, into official temple workers assisting the Levites, and was granted special status by the royal court, such as exemption from taxes.

introduce: Tola is a personal name referring to the ancestor of the Tola descendants, one of the clans of the tribe of Issachar, and there is no record in the Bible of a region called by this name.
biblecontents: These are the clans of the descendants of Issachar: from Tola, the Tola clan; from Puvah, the Punite clan; from Jashub, the Jashub clan; and from Shimron, the Shimron clan (Numbers 26:23-24)

introduce: The Leummites refers to a man recorded as a son of Dedan, who was born to Abraham and his concubine Keturah, or to the tribal group formed by his descendants.
biblecontents: They are mentioned as descendants born to Dedan, the son of Jokshan, the son whom Abraham fathered through Keturah (Genesis 25:3).
history: The Asshurites, the Letushites, and the Leummites, descendants of Dedan, are presumed to have settled in the northern or central part of Arabia in the ancient Near East and to have formed tribal states or commercial tribal groups. However, no concrete archaeological artifacts or inscriptions concerning a place or people called the Leummites have been clearly identified at the present time.

introduce: The Freedmen is a name mentioned in Acts 6:9, referring to a particular group of Jews living in Jerusalem made up of freed slaves or their descendants, or the name of the synagogue where they gathered.
biblecontents: Then some men from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, that is, the synagogue of the Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and those from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and argued with Stephen (Acts 6:9).
geography: At that time there were several synagogues in Jerusalem for Diaspora Jews, and the Synagogue of the Freedmen is presumed to have been one of them, located either inside the city of Jerusalem or in its vicinity.
history: Libertini is a term derived from the Latin libertinus, originally meaning slaves who had gained their freedom under the Roman legal system. After Pompey captured Jerusalem in 63 BC, many Jews were taken away as slaves of Rome, and it is interpreted that those who afterward gained their freedom and returned to Jerusalem formed a community centered on the Synagogue of the Freedmen.

introduce: Malchiel was a member of the tribe of Asher, one of the tribes of ancient Israel, and his descendants became the founders of a family called the Malchielite clan.
biblecontents: Malchiel is recorded as a grandson of Asher and a son of Beriah, and as the ancestor of the Malchielite clan that formed within the tribe of Asher (Numbers 26:45).
history: Malchiel is a figure belonging to the genealogy of Asher, a son of Jacob, and at the time of the census recorded in Numbers 26 he was established as a clan unit within the tribe of Asher (Numbers 26:45).

introduce: Malluchi is the name of a priestly family that appears in the book of Nehemiah and also the name of the office that the family carried out; it is one of the families that were active within the religious community of Jerusalem after the return from the exile.
biblecontents: Malluchi is mentioned as one of the heads of the priestly families in the time of Joiakim, and Jonathan carried out the priestly duties as representative of that family (Nehemiah 12:14).
history: The community of Israel that returned from the Babylonian exile reorganized the genealogies of the priestly families along with the restoration of temple worship, and the list recorded in Nehemiah 12, beginning with the high priest Jeshua, shows part of the historical process of establishing the succession of the priestly office and the genealogy of each family.

introduce: Mahli is a person belonging to the descendants of Merari, a branch of the tribe of Levi, and is an ancestor who formed that family.
biblecontents: Mahli is recorded as a son of Merari and the ancestor of the Merarite clan of the Levites (Numbers 3:33). Also, in the passage listing the genealogy of the Merarite clans, the descendants of Mahli are mentioned (Numbers 26:58).

introduce: Moadiah was one of the priestly families of the Jewish community in the time of the Persian empire, and is a figure mentioned in the process of the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the arrangement of its religious system after the return from the exile.
biblecontents: In the list of the heads of the priestly families in the time of Joiakim, it appears as "of Miniamin, that is, of the clan of Moadiah, Piltai" (Nehemiah 12:12, 17).
history: He is a figure who appears in the process of arranging the genealogies of the priestly families in the period when the wall of Jerusalem was being rebuilt after the return from the Babylonian exile. At that time the priestly families played a key role in restoring religious authority centered on the temple of Jerusalem and establishing order in the community.

introduce: Pelethites appears in the Bible as a term referring to a Pelethite and the Pelethites, a group mentioned as members of the Cherethites and the Pelethites, the royal guard organization of King David. Scholars presume that they were part of the Philistines or a group of mercenaries from the island of Crete.
biblecontents: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites (2 Samuel 8:18). When David fled, the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had come from Gath marched before the king (2 Samuel 15:18). Joab took the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men and pursued Sheba (2 Samuel 20:7). Benaiah was entrusted with the duty of commanding the Cherethites and the Pelethites (2 Samuel 20:23). When Solomon was enthroned, the priest Zadok, the prophet Nathan, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites brought Solomon down on the mount (1 Kings 1:38). The king sent Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they made Solomon ride on the king's mule and go up to the City of David (1 Kings 1:44). Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites (1 Chronicles 18:17).
geography: Scholars of the Old Testament link the Pelethites linguistically with the Philistines (Philistia), a place name associated with the island of Crete, and raise the possibility that they were a group of mercenaries originating from the Palestinian coastal region or the Mediterranean island region. The Bible does not state their exact place of residence, but they seem to have been stationed mainly in the royal palace at Jerusalem as the king's bodyguard.
history: King David, in order to consolidate his power, maintained a direct personal guard composed chiefly of foreign mercenaries, rather than a tribal army based on blood ties. The Cherethites and the Pelethites were trusted troops who accompanied him from the time of his early flight, and in the process of Solomon's succession to the throne they also functioned as a key military organization maintaining the stability and order of the royal house.

introduce: Shaul is the name referring to the Shaulite clan, one of the families of the tribe of Simeon.
biblecontents: Among the descendants of Simeon the Shaulite clan is mentioned, and they are a family formed through Shaul (Numbers 26:13).
history: It is a family name that appears in the process of classifying the clans of the tribe of Simeon by genealogy at the time of the census of Israel carried out on the plains of Moab.

introduce: Shuthelah is the name of the founder of the Shuthelahite family that is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim, and the name of a son of Ephraim.
biblecontents: The clans of the descendants of Ephraim are these: the Shuthelahite clan from Shuthelah, the Becher clan from Becher, and the Tahanite clan from Tahan (Numbers 26:35)
history: Shuthelah is recorded as a son of Ephraim, the second son of Joseph, the son of Jacob. In ancient Hebrew society the name of a family became the origin that formed a branch of that clan, and the existence of the Shuthelahite family within the tribe of Ephraim is confirmed through the census record of Numbers 26 (Numbers 26:35).

introduce: Shuham is the name of the chief of the tribe of Dan, one of the tribes of Israel, and also a proper noun referring to the clan of the tribe of Dan that was derived from him.
biblecontents: Shuham was a son of Dan and became the ancestor of the clan of Dan (Numbers 26:42). When Moses and the priest Eleazar took a census of the genealogy of the Israelites on the plains of Moab, the Shuhamite clan was mentioned (Numbers 26:43).
history: Shuham is recorded as Hushim in Genesis 46:23, but in Numbers 26 the name appears changed to Shuham. This is interpreted as a difference in the writing of a personal name arising from the process of copying in ancient Hebrew or from variation in oral tradition, and it is an example showing the genealogical classification of the early tribal society of Israel before the settlement in Canaan.

introduce: Shemaiah is a figure of a priestly family mentioned in connection with the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah, and is recorded as the name of the representative of a particular family, not as a particular place name.
biblecontents: Of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan (Nehemiah 12:18)
history: He is a figure included in the list of the priests who served at the dedication of the wall when the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt after the return from the Babylonian exile. This is one of the historical lists showing that the religious order centered on the temple of Jerusalem had been restored at that time.

introduce: Zemarites is the name referring to one branch of the Canaanite peoples, the descendants of Canaan.
biblecontents:
Canaan fathered Sidon and Heth, and also the Jebusite clan, the Amorite clan, the Girgashite clan, the Hivite clan, the Arkite clan, the Sinite clan, the Arvadite clan, the Zemarite clan, and the Hamathite clan; after this the clans of the descendants of Canaan were scattered (Genesis 10:18)
Canaan fathered Sidon and Heth, and also the Jebusite clan, the Amorite clan, the Girgashite clan, the Hivite clan, the Arkite clan, the Sinite clan, the Arvadite clan, the Zemarite clan, and the Hamathite clan (1 Chronicles 1:16)
geography: The Zemarite clan is presumed to have lived near Arvad in northern Syria on the Mediterranean coast. In ancient records they are also associated with an area known as Simra or Sumura.
history: Sumura, mentioned in Akkadian documents such as the Amarna letters, was an important port city and administrative center on the northern coast of ancient Phoenicia. This area was a strategic stronghold where power struggles between Egypt and the Hittites were frequent.

introduce: Zephon is a name referring to the ancestor of a family or tribe that appears in Numbers 26 of the Bible.
biblecontents: The Zephonite clan is mentioned among the clans of the descendants of Gad, which indicates that the person named Zephon was the founder of a particular family of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 26:15).

introduce: Simeon is the second son born to Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the tribe of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. In the process of the settlement in Canaan he received an allotment within the territory of the southern tribe of Judah, and he played a central role in the formation of the nation, in such matters as the census and the arrangement of the camp.
biblecontents: Simeon is mentioned, together with Levi, as one of the sons of Jacob (Exodus 6:15), and at the census at the time of the exodus Shelumiel was appointed as the commander of the tribe (Numbers 1:6). In the census of Numbers, the males of the tribe of Simeon numbered fifty-nine thousand three hundred (Numbers 1:23). During the march in the wilderness they belonged to the camp of Reuben and were positioned on the south (Numbers 2:12). For the spying out of Canaan, Shaphat son of Hori was chosen as a spy (Numbers 13:5), and in the incident of Baal-peor, an incident occurred in which Zimri, a leader of the tribe of Simeon, was involved with a Midianite woman (Numbers 25:14). After the census their number was recorded as twenty-two thousand two hundred (Numbers 26:14). Among the commanders appointed for the distribution of Canaan, the one from the descendants of Simeon was Shemuel (Numbers 34:20). Its name was listed among the tribes that were to bless the people on Mount Gerizim (Deuteronomy 27:12), and finally it was allotted its inheritance from within the inheritance of the descendants of Judah (Joshua 19:1).
geography: The tribe of Simeon was allotted territory centered on the Negev region in southern Canaan, but rather than forming an independent boundary, it took the form of being incorporated into the interior of the territory of the tribe of Judah. This is closely related, geographically, to the expansiveness and defense system of the tribe of Judah.
history: After the early period of settlement, the tribe of Simeon went through a process of political and military assimilation through its alliance with the tribe of Judah. Historically, they were gradually absorbed into the southern kingdom of Judah, lost their independent influence as a tribe, and had the social background of being regarded as a part of the tribe of Judah.

introduce: Zibeon is the name of one of the chiefs of the Horite clans who appear in the book of Genesis in the Old Testament, and it also means the name of the family in which he lived or exercised influence.
biblecontents: Zibeon is recorded as a chief of the Horite clans, whose descendants lived in the land of Seir (Genesis 36:29).
geography: They lived centered on the Seir hill country of the region of Edom and its surroundings, which includes the dry mountainous terrain of southern Jordan.

introduce: Apharsathchites is presumed to be a name referring to a people or a group of officials connected with an administrative district of the ancient Persian empire. It is one of the names for which no clear reality can be confirmed in records outside the Bible.
biblecontents: The Apharsathchites appear in the letter sent up to King Artaxerxes, and are mentioned as one of the many governors and officials of the Persian empire who drew up this letter (Ezra 4:9).
history: The Apharsathchites are thought to have been a group that existed within the administrative organization of the Persian empire under Artaxerxes I. In order to govern its vast territory, Persia integrated the officials and peoples of many regions into the central government and built an administrative network, and the names listed in the Bible are interpreted as the various ethnic and political units that formed part of this imperial administrative system (Ezra 4:9).

introduce: Asriel is a proper noun referring to a person who appears in Numbers 26 of the Bible and to a family of the tribe of Manasseh founded by him.
biblecontents: Asriel was a descendant of Gilead, the son of Manasseh, and the person who formed the Asrielite clan within the tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 26:31).
history: The family of Asriel was mentioned as one of the principal clans of the tribe of Manasseh when the Israelites carried out a census on the plains of Moab before the conquest of Canaan (Numbers 26:31). They are regarded as part of the half-tribe of Manasseh that was allotted the region of Gilead east of the Jordan.

introduce: Ashbel is one of the sons of Benjamin, the son of Jacob, and is a name referring to the founder of the Ashbelite clan, a family within the tribe of Benjamin.
biblecontents: Ashbel is mentioned as one of the sons of Benjamin, and his descendants formed the Ashbelite clan at the time of the census in Numbers (Numbers 26:38).
history: Within the genealogical system of the tribe of Benjamin, Ashbel is classed as one of the five sons of Benjamin, but there are slight differences in the names and number of the sons between the record of Genesis 46:21 and the record from 1 Chronicles 8:1 onward. This is analyzed as the result of the process of the formation and merging of families or branches being reflected in the way ancient Hebrew genealogies were recorded.

introduce: Ahiram is a person mentioned as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, and he appears as one of the sons of Benjamin in the list of the census of Israel recorded in Numbers 26.
biblecontents: The clans of the sons of Benjamin are these: the Belaite clan from Bela, the Ashbelite clan from Ashbel, and the Ahiramite clan from Ahiram (Numbers 26:38)
history: Ahiram is one of the figures who make up the genealogy of Benjamin, and he is specified as the ancestor of the Ahiramite clan within the tribe of Benjamin at the time of the census carried out as Israel was preparing for the wars of the conquest of Canaan after the exodus (Numbers 26:38). This is a historical record showing that Israelite society at that time was organized in a system of tribes and families.

introduce: Jamin is the name of a family of the tribe of Simeon, one of the twelve tribes of ancient Israel, and also the name of the ancestor who led that family.
biblecontents: The clans of the sons of Simeon are these: the Jaminite clan from Jamin and the Jachinite clan from Jachin (Numbers 26:12).
history: Jamin is recorded as a son of Simeon, the second son of Jacob, and shows that in the course of the census when the tribe of Simeon left Egypt and headed for Canaan, he had formed a single family unit.

introduce: Jashub is the ancestor of the Jashubite clan, a branch of the tribe of Issachar of Israel, and also means the name of the clan formed by that family.
biblecontents: Jashub was a son of Issachar, and from him the Jashubite clan began (Numbers 26:24).
history: In the process of settling in the land of Canaan after the exodus, the Jashubite clan was recorded through the census as one of the principal families of the tribe of Issachar.

introduce: Eran refers to the Eranite clan named after Eran, a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim.
biblecontents: Eran, a descendant of Shuthelah, the son of Ephraim, became the ancestor of the Eranite clan, and was recorded when Moses and the priest Eleazar took the census (Numbers 26:36).
history: It is a name mentioned through the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim at the time of the census carried out in the wilderness after the exodus, and is a record showing the social structure of the tribes of Israel and the formation of family units.

introduce: Eri is a person who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, and means the founder of the Erite clan, a branch of the tribe of Gad.
biblecontents: Eri is recorded as a son of Gad and the ancestor of the Erite clan, one of the families of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 26:16).
history: When the Israelites carried out a census on the plains of Moab after the exodus, he was classed as one of the detailed clans of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 26:16).

introduce: Eber is a personal name in the Bible referring to a descendant of Shem and an ancestor of Abraham, and at the same time, in Numbers 24:24, it is mentioned in the prophetic context that ships coming from the shores of Kittim would afflict Asshur and Eber, with the meaning of a geographical or ethnic base.
biblecontents: Shem was the father of all the children of Eber and the elder brother of Japheth (Genesis 10:21). Ships will come from the shore of Kittim and afflict Asshur and trouble Eber, but he too shall perish (Numbers 24:24).
geography: The exact location of Eber is difficult to specify as a detailed place name of the ancient Near East, but it is generally interpreted as being related to the migration route of the Semitic peoples moving west from the region of Mesopotamia. In the context of Numbers 24:24, it is also understood as a place name symbolizing the lowlands of the Euphrates or the eastern region.
history: Academically, Eber is regarded as the etymological basis of the Hebrew people, and carries the meaning of "those who crossed the river." In the record of Numbers, by being mentioned in parallel with Asshur, it is used as a name indicating a particular power or regional unit of the ancient Near East.

introduce: Jeshurun is a poetic and symbolic title in the Bible that refers to the people of Israel. By its Hebrew etymology it carries the meaning of "the upright one" or "the straight one," and it was used chiefly when emphasizing the faithfulness of the nation or its special relationship with God.
biblecontents: Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, bloated, and sleek; you abandoned God who made you and scorned the Rock of your salvation (Deuteronomy 32:15) There was a king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together (Deuteronomy 33:5) There is none like Jeshurun; He rides the heavens to help you, and the skies in His majesty (Deuteronomy 33:26) My servant Jacob, Jeshurun whom I have chosen, do not fear (Isaiah 44:2)
history: The name Jeshurun was devised as a term recalling the covenant relationship that ancient Israel had with God before and after its settlement in Canaan. Historically, it appears chiefly in the context of the Song of Moses and the account of the blessing in Deuteronomy, in which Israel's apostasy and God's protection are contrasted, and it was afterward carried on in the book of Isaiah as an expression emphasizing the identity of the nation. It does not refer to a particular place name, but is an idiomatic title referring to the whole national community called Israel.

introduce: Ozni refers to the Ozni clan of the tribe of Gad, one of the families of the tribes of Israel recorded in Numbers 26.
biblecontents: The Ozni clan is mentioned among the sons of Gad, and this is the record of the time when the census was carried out on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26:16).

introduce: Izhar is the name of the ancestor of the Izharites, one of the four families of the descendants of Kohath mentioned in Numbers 3:27, and refers to the clan they formed. As a branch of the tribe of Levi, it was a group genealogically classified in order to carry out duties connected with the service of the tabernacle.
biblecontents: From Kohath were born Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel; these are the clans of Kohath (Numbers 3:27)
history: Izhar is the second son of Kohath, the son of Levi. The descendants of Kohath were given the task of looking after and carrying the furnishings of the tabernacle after the exodus, and the descendants of Izhar were likewise constituted as a clan unit within this system. At the time of the record of Numbers 3, the clan of the descendants of Izhar camped on the south side of the tabernacle and was assigned a share of responsibility for the care of the tabernacle furnishings.

introduce: Iezer refers to a person belonging to the Abiezer family of the tribe of Manasseh who appears in the book of Numbers in the Old Testament, and to the name of the clan that family formed.
biblecontents: In the census carried out by the Israelites before entering Canaan, he is recorded as a descendant of Abiezer, the son of Gilead (Numbers 26:30).
history: The census recorded in Numbers 26 was carried out on the second generation of the exodus in order to prepare for the distribution of the land of Canaan, and Iezer is mentioned as a member of the genealogical unit connected with the distribution of inheritances east or west of the Jordan, as a detailed clan of the tribe of Manasseh.

introduce: Hebrew appears in the Bible chiefly as the name of a people referring to the descendants of Abraham, and was used as a term expressing their identity as foreigners during the time of their sojourn in Egypt.
biblecontents: Abram was called a Hebrew (Genesis 14:13), and when Joseph was in servitude in Egypt, he referred to his origin as the land of the Hebrews (Genesis 40:15). Joseph's wife and master called him a Hebrew (Genesis 39:14, Genesis 39:17), and Pharaoh's officials called him a Hebrew servant (Genesis 41:12). The Egyptians considered it unclean to eat with the Hebrews (Genesis 43:32), and the Egyptian midwives were mentioned as those who assisted the Hebrew women in childbirth (Exodus 1:15, Exodus 1:19). The princess of Egypt identified the child found in the Nile as a Hebrew baby (Exodus 2:6). Pharaoh gave the command to throw the sons of the Hebrews into the Nile (Exodus 1:16).
geography: The land of the Hebrews that Joseph mentioned is interpreted as referring to the region of Canaan, which was the place where the family of Abraham originated, geographically distinct from Egypt.
history: The term Hebrew is also discussed as having an etymological connection with the Habiru or Apiru of the ancient Near East. Historically, it is possible that it was used as a term for wandering groups that had not settled or for the lowest class of society. During the time of the sojourn in Egypt, the name Hebrew functioned as a name signifying social marginalization, or "othering," by which the Egyptians, the majority people, distinguished a minority group of foreign laborers.
